quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What danger does wind noise create?

options.text: It is easy to get used to.
It can cause permanent hearing damage.
It is never dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can cause permanent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Long exposure to wind noise can permanently damage your hearing. Wear ear plugs or other hearing protection when riding.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Right lane ends
Left lane ends
Traffic control device ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black letters or symbols. This sign warns you that the right lane will end ahead.

questions.question: Where should your feet be when riding?

options.text: On the gas tank.
Hanging loose.
On the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the footrests.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet on the footrests while riding. This helps you maintain balance.

questions.question: How should your jacket and pants fit when riding?

options.text: Loose enough for wind to catch the fabric.
Snug enough so they do not flap in the wind.
Tight enough to restrict your movement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snug enough so they do not flap in the wind.
questions.explanation: Your jacket and pants should fit snugly so they do not flap, but also loose enough to let you move freely.

questions.question: What should you do to stop quickly?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use the front brake first.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Apply controlled pressure to both the front and rear brakes at the same time. Be careful not to lock the brakes.

questions.question: Which lane position should you choose?

options.text: One that makes you visible and gives you safe space around your motorcycle.
Whatever position you prefer, without thinking about other drivers.
One that puts you close to other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: One that makes you visible and gives you safe space around your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Position yourself where other drivers can see you and where you have space around your motorcycle. Change your position as road conditions change.

questions.question: Why is your lane position important when riding?

options.text: It does not affect whether other drivers can see you.
It affects whether other drivers can see you.
It cannot protect you from wind blasts.

questions.correctAnswerText: It affects whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen. It also helps you avoid wind blasts from other vehicles.

questions.question: What should you do before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle?

options.text: Just start riding. Learning by doing is best.
Just start riding. All bikes are the same.
Practice using the throttle, clutch, and brakes to learn how it works.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice using the throttle, clutch, and brakes to learn how it works.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Do a safety check, find where everything is located, and practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding.

questions.question: What should you do when you see an emergency vehicle stopped on the road with flashing lights?

options.text: Stop on the roadway behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait for the emergency vehicle to move.
Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes to give it extra space and proceed with caution. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What should you do if you ride on a slippery surface?

options.text: Slow down
Speed up
Make sudden movements

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, reduce your speed and avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes carefully.

questions.question: What is the danger of improper braking?

options.text: It usually has no consequences.
It causes many motorcycle crashes.
It is not a concern because motorcycles have two brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: It causes many motorcycle crashes.
questions.explanation: Improper braking causes many motorcycle crashes. Using correct braking technique is an important part of safe riding.

questions.question: What can happen from long-term exposure to wind noise?

options.text: It is not dangerous.
It can permanently damage your hearing.
It is just a normal part of riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can permanently damage your hearing.
questions.explanation: Long-term exposure to wind noise can permanently damage your hearing. Wear ear protection when riding. Good ear protection lets you hear important sounds like sirens and car horns.

questions.question: How do you get the most protection from your helmet?

options.text: Make sure it fits snugly.
Keep it clean.
Choose one that looks cool.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure it fits snugly.
questions.explanation: Your helmet gives you the most protection when it meets DOT and state safety standards, fits snugly all the way around, and has no visible damage.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet
Lanes shift
Yield

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that the road ahead is slippery when wet.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.
Only stop to let other traffic pass.
Vehicles will be entering the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, let all crossing traffic and pedestrians pass, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should you wear?

options.text: Always wear a jacket.
Wear a jacket only at night.
Wear a jacket only when it is cold.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear a jacket.
questions.explanation: Always wear a sturdy jacket with long sleeves when riding, even in warm weather.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of head or neck injury?

options.text: By wearing a helmet.
By riding slowly.
By reading the owner's manual.

questions.correctAnswerText: By wearing a helmet.
questions.explanation: Head and neck injuries are a risk at any speed. A quality helmet, worn properly, greatly reduces this risk.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: The driver may need your lane to pass.
You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
You will have access to escape routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding directly next to another vehicle is dangerous because the driver cannot see you in their blind spot. The vehicle may also block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: What should you check when choosing a helmet?

options.text: That it has no cracks or defects.
That it looks nice.
That it fits loosely.

questions.correctAnswerText: That it has no cracks or defects.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT and state safety standards. It should fit snugly and be free of damage like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: What should a motorcycle rider do to reduce collision chances?

options.text: Keep enough space between your bike and other vehicles.
Ride very slowly.
Ride on the centerline.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep enough space between your bike and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: To reduce collision risk, always maintain adequate space around your motorcycle. Keep this space when following, being followed, passing, being passed, or sharing a lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No left turn
No U-turn
No right turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers about traffic laws for that area. This sign means you cannot turn right.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, it is important to:

options.text: Focus only on what is in front of you.
Focus only on what is behind you.
Know what's happening both in front of and behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know what's happening both in front of and behind you.
questions.explanation: Watch what is ahead of you and what is behind you. Check your mirrors often to stay aware of traffic around you.

questions.question: You have a better chance of avoiding serious injury in a crash if you wear:

options.text: Face or eye protection.
A baseball cap.
Sneakers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Face or eye protection.
questions.explanation: A helmet is your best protection from injury. A plastic face shield that won't shatter helps protect your face in a crash.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Only protects your eyes.
Helps protect your whole face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps protect your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your entire face. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: When a motorcyclist needs to stop quickly, they should:

options.text: Apply both brakes at the same time.
Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes together to stop quickly. Look ahead to avoid sudden stops.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Should only be used in an emergency.
Should be used with the rear brake.
Is unsafe to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be used with the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: If you approach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle:

options.text: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
You should flash your headlight to signal that the other vehicle should proceed.
You should continue through the intersection and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or lights, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: When riding in a group, riders should:

options.text: All maintain safe following distances.
Follow each other as closely as possible.
Not worry about distances between members.

questions.correctAnswerText: All maintain safe following distances.
questions.explanation: Ride in a staggered formation. This keeps riders close together while maintaining safe distances between motorcycles.

questions.question: The faster you drink alcohol:

options.text: The faster the alcohol is removed from your body.
The faster the alcohol accumulates in your body.
The less the alcohol affects your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: The faster the alcohol accumulates in your body.
questions.explanation: Drinking quickly causes alcohol to build up in your body. Your body removes about one drink per hour. If you drink more than one drink per hour, alcohol stays in your system.

questions.question: When cars are merging from an entrance ramp:

options.text: A motorcyclist should assume the entering drivers see them.
A motorcyclist should never assume the entering drivers see them.
A motorcyclist should stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcyclist should never assume the entering drivers see them.
questions.explanation: Give merging cars plenty of space. Do not assume they see you. Change lanes if possible. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to let them merge safely.
